### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `af2bfae226ea4a123eb866566815c3a96eec2ac2` — the merge of head `4e057d908e16aae99375c697f7420e789ffc5344` into base `12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin af2bfae226ea4a123eb866566815c3a96eec2ac2 && git checkout af2bfae226ea4a123eb866566815c3a96eec2ac2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267 4e057d908e16aae99375c697f7420e789ffc5344 && git checkout -B drift-repro 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267 && git merge --no-ff 4e057d908e16aae99375c697f7420e789ffc5344

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 12b9daf7493f30ebb5faf47e7b40eb99d2bda267` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4e057d908e16aae99375c697f7420e789ffc5344`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-10-11T14:33Z on card #22790 (triage 6106471041, claim 6108682129, the os-dev-report), the two #6017 declarations (6108690316, 6110016343), PR #22857's body, file list and net diff against `main` at the merge-base `c4e7fa5a31`, the #20487 precedent where it declared the pair on `EngineAggregateOptionsSchema`, and the check-runs on this head. Read-only: `git diff` / `git show` / `git grep` / `git merge-tree` against fetched shas, `gh api` reads; nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **One expander — right.** `count()` (engine.ts 18691) runs `foldEngineOptionAliases` → `rejectUnknownEngineOptions` → `lowerWhereFilterArray` → `expandSearchOnOptions` (12700), which carries `{ object, where, search, searchFields }` into the one `expandSearchOnAst` (12633) that `find` calls at 12859 and `aggregate` reaches through the same helper at 18837. Same schema source (`this._registry.getObject(object)`), same `collectInternalReadFields` withhold of `internal: true` columns, same `searchableFields` / `nameField ?? displayNameField` resolution, same `requestedFields = searchFields ?? raw.fields` narrowing intersected never widened. Sequence position matches `aggregate` exactly (after the `where` doors, before the AST, token resolution and middleware); `find` differs only in that it runs `fillQueryAstDefaults` first, and that is inert for `search`, which is deliberately not parsed (12743). A `searchFields`-only bag or a `null` search takes the same no-expansion path on every verb. The helper is the #20487 `expandSearchOnAggregateOptions` generalised over `T extends EngineAggregateOptions | EngineCountOptions`; no second expander exists, and the door pin's one-expander case asserts the driver COUNT `where` deep-equals the driver FIND `where`.
- **Middleware-scoped count — right.** `opCtx.ast = { object, where: query?.where }` is built from the expanded bag (18709), `resolveWhereTokens` runs on it, the security middlewares inject into `opCtx.ast.where`, and `driver.count` receives `opCtx.ast` (18734). The `find().length` fallback passes `callerWhere` (captured after expansion, before middleware, 18725) with no `search` key, so `find` scopes it itself and never re-expands. Door pin: member sees `total: 25` of 75; dev ablation A4 went red in the predicted direction.
- **`findData` paged arm — right.** `const countable = options.search == null` and the `else` estimate arm (`total = pageOffset + records.length + (hasMore ? 1 : 0)`) are deleted. The count call carries `where`, `search`, `searchFields`, `context` — the same `options.search` / `options.searchFields` the `find` call received, after `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` and `narrowStoredMetadataSearch` (13005–13023), so the count narrows exactly as the rows do. `hasMore = pageOffset + records.length < counted` agrees with `total` by construction. The `countOptOut` arm is unchanged (`total = undefined`, `hasMore` from the page). The degraded-count `catch` (`counted = pageOffset + records.length`) is byte-unchanged, per triage. The two tests that pinned the estimate are flipped to the counted shape, and the zero-limit pin now asserts the COUNT carries the same `search` the FIND did.
- **Schema members — right.** `search: z.union([z.string(), FullTextSearchSchema]).optional()` and `searchFields: z.array(z.string()).optional()` are byte-identical to `EngineQueryOptionsSchema` (144, 153) and to the #20487 declaration on `EngineAggregateOptionsSchema` (448, 454). `data-engine.test.ts` pins JSON-schema equality of both keys against the query options. `EngineCountOptionsParsed = z.infer` is declared beside `EngineCountOptions = z.input` because `FullTextSearchSchema` carries flag defaults, so input and infer part — ADR-0122's condition — and the isomorphism pin `Iso_data_dataEngine__EngineCountOptionsSchema` leaves (776 → 775), the same shape #20487 took (780 → 779). The deprecated `DataEngineCountOptionsSchema` is left unwidened, as #20487 left its legacy sibling. Generated: `api-surface` +1 type, `authorable-surface` +2 keys, `export-origins` +1, `data-engine.mdx` rows; nothing removed or narrowed.
- **`ENGINE_COUNT_OPTION_KEYS` and the refusal — right.** The set is `{ context, where, search, searchFields }`; `rejectUnknownEngineOptions` is untouched. The drift pin `engine-unknown-option.test.ts:264` (`expectSetMatches('count', EngineCountOptionsSchema, [])`) derives the legal set from the schema with no documented extras, so set and schema stay equal — and that pin is what makes the spec the only route, which is the PR's Clause-② argument; it holds. No test pins the old count legal-key message (none found by `git grep`). The `bogus` / `tenantId` refusal pins for `count` are unchanged.
- **`HookCountQuery` — right.** `Omit<EngineCountOptions, 'context'>` widens by derivation. Both TSDoc sites are corrected (the method-group note and the type's own doc) and both now read true against the engine constant. `hook-api.test.ts` KEPT `['where','search','searchFields']` / OMITTED `['context']` equals the Omit. The runtime face honours it: `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts:995` forwards the bag whole to `ql.count(objectName, withCtx(opts))`, so the changeset's "`ctx.api.object(name).count()` accepts the two keys" is true, not just typed.
- **`DataEngineCountRequestSchema` — docs only, right as left.** Its `query` is `EngineCountOptionsSchema.extend(RpcLegacyFilterMixin)`, so it inherits the pair. `git grep` at this head finds no reader of `DataEngineCountRequestSchema` / `DataEngineRequestSchema` outside `packages/spec` except the generated references (`data-engine.mdx`, `references/index.mdx`). No door widens through it today; should a reader appear, what it admits is exactly what `engine.count` executes, so it cannot become a silent drop. The dev's acceptance note states this correctly.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/22790-search-total-counted.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor**, `@objectstack/objectql` **minor**, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` **patch**; carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and FROM `count(object, { where })` → TO `count(object, { where, search, searchFields })`. Right on every row.
- spec: two additive optional members on a published accept set plus one added type export → minor, as required by `yes`. objectql: `engine.count` (the published `IDataEngine.count` function schema, zod 540–542) now honours keys it refused as unknown options → an accept-set widening, minor. metadata-protocol: the wire accept set does not move (`$search` with `$top` was accepted before); what moves is the value of `total` from a page-local estimate to the declared meaning of `FindDataResponse.total` ("Total number of records matching the filter"), and `hasMore` on an exactly-full last page from `true` to `false` → a fix, patch.
- **Not a narrowing anyone could rely on.** The response schema is unchanged (`total?: number`, `hasMore: boolean`); a client that relied on `total == offset + page + 1` relied on the defect against the field's own description, and a client paging until `hasMore === false` now stops one empty page earlier. The one cost that moves — a COUNT with LIKE arms is issued under a search where none was — is the cost triage accepted, and `$count=false` stays the opt-out, unchanged.
- Skew: spec, objectql, metadata-protocol and rest sit in one `fixed` group in `.changeset/config.json`, so the four bump together to the group's minor. A metadata-protocol that sends `search` to the count cannot ship against an objectql that refuses it (that pairing would land in the untouched `catch` and answer `hasMore: false` on every page).
- The PR's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` agrees with the changeset, the claim (6108682129) and both declarations. Triage's `Clause-②: no` was superseded by the claim's measured reading and the arm is correct: the count option schema is a published accept set and it grows. `Check Changeset` and `Spec property liveness` concluded success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation (1)** — spec files beyond the first declaration: ruled **A** (6110016343). The diff holds exactly the ruled set: `hook-api.ts` (TSDoc only, +4/−3), `hook-api.test.ts`, `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`, `data-engine.test.ts`. No further spec source file. Within the ruling.
- **Dev deviation (2)** — `searchFields` beside `search`: ruled **A**. The declaration is byte-identical to the #20487 precedent, and the measured reason holds in the code: `findData` narrows `options.searchFields` before both calls, so a count given `search` alone would over-count on stored-metadata tables. Within the ruling.
- **Dev deviation (3)** — +301/−62 over 15 files against the 300 suggestion: `Check PR Size` concluded success. 157 added lines are the real-chain door pin, 25 generated, 17 changeset; source is +61/−42 across four files. Noted, no action.
- **Dev deviation (4)** — `origin/main` not merged in: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 4e057d908e` with main at `12b9daf7` is clean (exit 0, no conflicts). `protocol.ts` did move on main since the merge-base — PR #22833 (`8c105e3d67`, merged 2026-10-11T13:52Z), boot-report and TSDoc regions — and merge-tree against #22833's head is clean. PR #22819 (open draft, `a1ed7388`, the `engine.ts` write doors) merge-trees clean against this head too. One stale sentence: the PR body and the dev report say neither neighbour had landed and name main as `d8c7d38648`, but #22833 had merged and main was at `12b9daf7` (2026-10-11T13:48Z) before the PR opened (2026-10-11T14:20Z). The CI `pull_request` runs were created after both, so their merge ref includes them. A stale sentence, not a conflict.
- **Dev deviation (5)** — commit trailers: all four commits carry the AGENTS.md model-free pair (`Claude-Session:` plus the plain Claude co-author line); the harness reminder's model-named trailer is the one the pre-push hook refuses. Right as done.
- **Dev deviation (6)** — the verify lock held 21m54s on the spec repo-tier run: process note, no contract effect.
- **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally** (exit 3, prerequisite — 44 packages outside the closure unbuilt). The check-run that answers it is **`Build Core`** (`ci.yml` job `build-core`, step "Every published require entry point actually loads"), and it concluded **success** on this head. The dev's narrowed 22-entry probe is a dev-side measurement, not the gate.
- **Check-runs on this head as read:** concluded success — Auto Label, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, filter; skipped (opt-in) — Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke; **still in progress** — Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3) and (3/3), Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core (1/6)–(6/6), Type Check · workspace. Only what concluded is judged here; the queue leg needs every check green regardless of this record, and this record does not wait on them.
- **Governed surfaces:** none in the file list (`.changeset/`, `content/docs/references/`, `packages/**`); Governed Surface Queue Guard success.
- **Published skill row understates the set, outside this card:** `skills/objectstack-query/SKILL.md:27` lists engine `count`'s legal keys as `context`, `where`; after this PR the closed set also holds `search`, `searchFields` — the same class as #20487's acceptance note on the aggregate row. Nothing it names is refused. `skills/**` is Tier H; carrier is the seat, as a docs-only edit on its own PR. Not a defect of this diff.
- Pre-existing, unchanged: the `as any` on the count bag in `findData` (erasure baseline, now carrying only declared keys), and the engine's unknown-option refusal being a bare `Error` with no ADR-0112 code.
